purpose: Teach: 蛇足/悪し/男前/わが子/惨め/見分ける/読み取る/老若男女

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは蛇足な事を言わない方だった
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, your father wasn't one to say unnecessary things.
lines.style: Soft, gazing inward. Warm nostalgia colors each word. Slow unhurried pace, as if remembering something vivid. Slight pause before "unnecessary" — choosing the right word matters.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、悪しき慣習を改めようとされたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, Grandpa — he really did work to change old, harmful ways, didn't he?
lines.style: Bright affirmation with underlying pride. The question at the end is rhetorical, almost musical — she's reminding him of something they both know. Warm, collaborative tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは「男前」と評判だった
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, your father had quite a reputation. They called him handsome.
lines.style: A small smile in the voice. Tender but with quiet dignity. Pace is measured and even. The compliment lands gently — not boasting, simply remembering.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、わが子のために生涯尽くされたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa, he gave his whole life to his own children, didn't he?
lines.style: Gentle assertion, almost meditative. She's not asking for confirmation — she's witnessing alongside him. Warm, knowing tone with deep contentment underneath.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが惨めな思いをした日もあった
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, there were days when your father felt ashamed.
lines.style: Quieter now, with tender sorrow. The words come slowly, carefully — he's trusting her with something fragile. Breathiness on "ashamed." No judgment, only witness.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お孫様の表情を見分けるのが上手だったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa, he was always so good at seeing what his grandchildren were really feeling, wasn't he?
lines.style: Soft recognition tinged with longing. She's gently correcting the frame — turning his pain into the gift he gave. Tender, almost healing tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが手紙の行間を読み取る方だった
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, your father was the kind of man who could read between the lines of a letter.
lines.style: Deep respect in the voice. A long, deliberate breath before "between the lines." This is a quiet marvel — the sensitivity it took. Slow, reverent pace.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、村祭りでは老若男女と分け隔てなく接したわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa, at the village festivals he treated everyone the same, young and old alike, didn't he?
lines.style: Warm certainty with quiet joy. The catalogue of his kindness isn't boastful — it's a gift she's giving him, reminding him of who he was. Close and intimate, like sharing a secret.
